content.title: Welcome aboard
content.description: Welcome to the course! This section will introduce you to the basics of programming and set the foundation for your learning journey.

content.title: What is Programming?
content.description: Programming is the process of writing instructions for computers to perform specific tasks. It involves problem-solving, logic, and creativity.

content.title: Flowcharts and Pseudocode
content.description: Flowcharts and pseudocode are tools to help you plan and visualize your programs before writing actual code. They make it easier to understand and debug your logic.

content.title: Programming Languages
content.description: There are many programming languages, such as Python, Java, C++, and JavaScript. Each language has its strengths and is suited for different types of projects.

content.title: Setting Up Your Environment
content.description: Learn how to install and set up a code editor, compiler, and other tools required for programming.

content.title: Basics of Data Structures
content.description: Data structures are ways to organize and store data efficiently. Common data structures include arrays, linked lists, stacks, and queues.

content.title: Arrays
content.description: Arrays are collections of elements stored in contiguous memory locations. They are useful for storing and accessing data in a structured way.

content.title: Linked Lists
content.description: Linked lists are dynamic data structures where each element (node) points to the next. They are useful for insertions and deletions.

content.title: Stacks and Queues
content.description: Stacks follow the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle, while queues follow the First-In-First-Out (FIFO) principle. Both are used in various algorithms and applications.

content.title: Introduction to Algorithms
content.description: Algorithms are step-by-step procedures for solving problems. Examples include sorting, searching, and graph traversal algorithms.

content.title: Sorting Algorithms
content.description: Learn about popular sorting algorithms like Bubble Sort, Quick Sort, and Merge Sort, and understand their time and space complexities.

content.title: Searching Algorithms
content.description: Explore algorithms like Linear Search and Binary Search, and learn how to efficiently find elements in a dataset.

content.title: What is OOP?
content.description: Object-Oriented Programming is a programming paradigm that uses objects and classes to structure code. It emphasizes reusability, modularity, and scalability.

content.title: Classes and Objects
content.description: A class is a blueprint for creating objects, while an object is an instance of a class. Learn how to define classes and create objects in your code.

content.title: Inheritance
content.description: Inheritance allows a class to inherit properties and methods from another class. It promotes code reuse and hierarchical classification.

content.title: Polymorphism
content.description: Polymorphism allows objects to take on multiple forms. It enables methods to behave differently based on the object that invokes them.

content.title: Encapsulation
content.description: Encapsulation is the concept of bundling data and methods that operate on that data within a single unit (class). It ensures data security and integrity.

content.title: Abstraction
content.description: Abstraction involves hiding complex implementation details and exposing only the necessary features of an object. It simplifies code and reduces complexity.

content.title: Recursion
content.description: Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem. It is commonly used in algorithms like tree traversal and divide-and-conquer.

content.title: Dynamic Programming
content.description: Dynamic Programming is a method for solving complex problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems. It is used in optimization problems.

content.title: Graph Algorithms
content.description: Graphs are data structures that represent relationships between objects. Learn about algorithms like Depth-First Search (DFS) and Breadth-First Search (BFS).

content.title: Big O Notation
content.description: Big O Notation is used to describe the performance or complexity of an algorithm. It helps you analyze the efficiency of your code.

content.title: Design Patterns
content.description: Design patterns are reusable solutions to common software design problems. Examples include Singleton, Factory, and Observer patterns.

content.title: Concurrency and Multithreading
content.description: Concurrency involves executing multiple tasks simultaneously. Learn how to write multithreaded programs to improve performance.
